newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Investbanka posts 1.9 mln dinar profit in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Investbanka posts 1.9 mln dinar profit in 1996.

text.p: Yugoslavia's Investbanka AD reported on Thursday a 1.962 million dinar ($341,898) net profit in 1996 and said it plans to increase its 1997 net earnings to 7.38 million dinars.

"Despite operating under difficult conditions, overall illiquidity and troubles in collecting its debt, Investbanka posted a profit in 1996," the bank's general manager Nikola Stanic told an annual shareholders meeting.
"But this year we expect better results and profits of around 7.5 million dinars," Stanic said.
Shareholders agreed that the bank, instead of paying out dividends, direct the profits to its reserves. Investbanka's 1996 reserves stood at 149.374 million dinars.
The bank's auditors Deloitte & Touche recommended to Investbanka to build up its reserves and prepare for servicing its share in the country's foreign debt.
According to the bank's sources, Investbanka holds 33 percent of the entire foreign debt of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, unofficially estimated at around $9 billion.

Ranked at the top of 116 Yugoslav banks by the amount of permanent capital, Investbanka said it increased its permanent capital to 1.199 billion dinars from 754 million in 1995. Its assets grew 14 percent to 10.9 billion dinars, Stanic said.
For 1997, the bank said it was negotiating to take part in the economic revival of Republika Srpska (the Bosnian Serb Republic).

The bank has already extended 90 million dinars out of 350 million planned for various reconstruction works in the region, Stanic told the bank's shareholders. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
